newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain adjourns ruling on two Qatari spy suspects.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain adjourns ruling on two Qatari spy suspects.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court on Wednesday postponed ruling on a Qatari man and woman accused of spying to December 25, an official said.

The trial of Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri began on December 4. They were accused of gathering intelligence for the Qatari government and accepting money from Doha to undermine Bahrain's security.
If convicted, they could face execution or long prison terms. Qatar has denied they were spies.

"The State Security Court decided to postpone its ruling on the two Qatari suspects for spying for Qatar to December 25," the official said. Relatives of the defendants attended Wednesday's court session, he said.
Qatar has accused Bahrain of torturing al-Baker and said the trial set a dangerous precedent in Gulf ties. Bahrain has denied the torture accusation.
The charges have raised tensions between Bahrain and Qatar, already in dispute over small islands controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
